Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Moët & Chandon: The Champagne house's Dom Pérignon is named for a monk, and Napoleon was a famous customer.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Hennessy: Founded by an Irish officer in the French town of Cognac, it is the world's biggest cognac brand.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Jameson: The Dublin distillery, founded by a Scot, makes its whiskey by triple distillation.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Johnnie Walker: A Kilmarnock grocer's name became a whisky giant, with its square bottle and slanted label.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Bacardi: A bat logo adorns this rum, founded in Santiago de Cuba, and the bat was said to bring luck.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Aperol: Born in Padua, the bright orange bittersweet aperitif is the base for the Spritz.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Jägermeister: Its name means master hunter, its logo is a stag with a cross, and it blends 56 herbs and spices.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Baileys: The first Irish cream liqueur combined whiskey and cream in a drink that keeps on the shelf.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Absolut Vodka: The Swedish vodka's bottle was inspired by an old pharmacy bottle, and Warhol painted it in 1985.
Wine and spirits brands, by founding yea.Grey Goose: Sidney Frank invented this brand, and Bacardi bought it for about 2 billion dollars in 2004.

Animal-star movies by release.Lassie Come Home: This film made the collie a star; the lead dog, Pal, was male, and his descendants played the role for generations.
Animal-star movies by release.Old Yeller: Disney's tearful Texas frontier story helped make 'Old Yeller' a byword for a sad dog ending.
Animal-star movies by release.Benji: Made on a tiny budget, this scruffy-dog film became a sleeper hit; the star dog, Higgins, had come from an animal shelter.
Animal-star movies by release.Turner & Hooch: Tom Hanks's costar was a dogue de Bordeaux, a French mastiff breed known for being huge, slobbery and loyal.
Animal-star movies by release.Beethoven: The title St. Bernard comes from a breed developed at an Alpine hospice to rescue travellers lost in the snow.
Animal-star movies by release.Free Willy: The orca actor Keiko was real, and the film's success sparked a campaign to free him from a cramped Mexican tank.
Animal-star movies by release.Babe: Real pigs plus animatronics played the sheep-herding hero, and the film won an Oscar for its visual effects.
Animal-star movies by release.Air Bud: The golden retriever Buddy could really shoot hoops, and the film spawned a long run of sequels.
Animal-star movies by release.Marley & Me: Based on journalist John Grogan's memoir, the Labrador title role was shared by more than 20 dogs.
Animal-star movies by release.A Dog's Purpose: Based on W. Bruce Cameron's novel, it follows one soul reincarnated through several dogs, each with its own owner.

When these companies filed for bankruptc.Penn Central: Formed by a 1968 railroad merger, in 1970 it filed what was then the largest bankruptcy in US history.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.Texaco: It filed after losing a judgment of over ten billion dollars to Pennzoil in a dispute over the Getty Oil takeover.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.Pan Am: Once the world's biggest international airline and a pioneer of jumbo jets; the 1988 Lockerbie bombing damaged it.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.Polaroid: Its instant film symbolised instant photography, and the brand was later revived by others.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.General Motors: In 2009 it was one of the largest industrial bankruptcies in US history, and the government took a majority stake.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.Blockbuster: It once had thousands of stores, and it reportedly passed on a chance to buy Netflix for $50 million in 2000.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.Borders: Its 2011 closure ended the big-box bookstore era; it had outsourced online sales to Amazon until 2008.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.Kodak: It invented the digital camera in 1975 yet filed in 2012; it emerged in 2013.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.Toys \"R\" Us: Its giraffe mascot was called Geoffrey; after the bankruptcy, the brand was revived by others.
When these companies filed for bankruptc.WeWork: Once valued at around $47 billion in 2019, it filed for bankruptcy in November 2023.

The 1980s, one event per year.Solidarity founded in Poland: Founded at the Gdansk shipyard under Lech Walesa, it was the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc.
The 1980s, one event per year.Reagan shot: John Hinckley Jr. shot the president outside a Washington hotel, and Reagan reportedly joked to surgeons that he hoped they were Republicans.
The 1980s, one event per year.Falklands War: Argentina's invasion of British islands in the South Atlantic led to a ten-week war, ending with Britain retaking them.
The 1980s, one event per year.Korean Air 007 shot down: A Soviet fighter shot down the Boeing 747 that had strayed into Soviet airspace, killing all 269 aboard; it led Reagan to open GPS for civilian use.
The 1980s, one event per year.Bhopal gas disaster: A leak of toxic gas from a Union Carbide pesticide plant in India killed thousands, making it among the worst industrial disasters ever.
The 1980s, one event per year.Gorbachev takes power: His policies of glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring) set in motion changes that led to the end of the Soviet Union.
The 1980s, one event per year.Chernobyl disaster: Reactor 4 exploded during a safety test in Ukraine; the exclusion zone around it now teems with wildlife.
The 1980s, one event per year.Black Monday crash: The Dow dropped about 22 percent in a single day, still the largest one-day percentage fall in its history.
The 1980s, one event per year.Lockerbie bombing: Pan Am Flight 103 exploded over a Scottish town, killing 270 people, in the deadliest terrorist attack in UK history.
The 1980s, one event per year.Berlin Wall falls: A mistaken announcement about travel rules sent crowds to the border, and the Wall that had divided the city for 28 years opened that night.

Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.First social smile: Early newborn grins are reflexes; a true social smile answers a caregiver's face, and it is often the first moment parents feel their baby is communicating.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Holds head steady: A newborn's head is a quarter of its body length, so steady neck control, built by tummy time, is one of the first big motor skills.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Sits without support: Most babies start with propping on their hands, and then sit alone, a milestone that frees the hands to grab and explore objects.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Crawls: Many babies skip classic crawling and instead scoot on their bottoms or roll, and it doesn't signal any trouble in development.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Walks alone: First steps typically come around the first birthday, though perfectly healthy toddlers may start walking anywhere between about 9 and 18 months.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Two-word phrases: Vocabulary typically leaps from a few words to hundreds in the second year, in what's often called the 'word spurt'.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Loses first baby tooth: Children typically lose all 20 baby teeth between about 6 and 12, replaced by 32 adult teeth, and the first to go are usually the bottom front ones.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Puberty begins: This stage, triggered by hormones from the brain, starts earlier in girls on average, and has shifted a little earlier in many countries over the past century.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Wisdom teeth come in: They're called third molars, and many people lack room for them, which is why wisdom teeth are among the most commonly removed teeth.
Baby and child milestones, by typical ag.Prefrontal cortex matures: The brain's front region, which handles planning and impulse control, is the last area to mature, around the mid-20s, which helps to explain teenage risk-taking.

When these Nintendo machines launched.Color TV-Game: The Color TV-Game was Nintendo's first home console, and it played variations of Pong, from the days when the company still sold playing cards.
When these Nintendo machines launched.Game & Watch: Game & Watch was created by Gunpei Yokoi after he saw a bored businessman playing with a calculator, and it led to the D-pad.
When these Nintendo machines launched.Famicom (NES): The Famicom was released in Japan as a red-and-white machine, and it was reborn overseas as the NES, which rescued the video game industry.
When these Nintendo machines launched.Super Famicom (SNES): The Super Famicom came with Super Mario World, and its controller added shoulder buttons and four face buttons.
When these Nintendo machines launched.Nintendo 64: The Nintendo 64 had a controller with an analog stick, and it was the first console to be designed with 3D games in mind.
When these Nintendo machines launched.GameCube: The GameCube used small discs rather than standard DVDs and came in a bright purple color.
When these Nintendo machines launched.Wii: The Wii's motion controls brought non-gamers into games, and it sold over 100 million units.
When these Nintendo machines launched.Wii U: The Wii U was a console with a tablet controller, and it was a commercial failure, but many of its games found success on Switch.
When these Nintendo machines launched.Nintendo Switch: The Switch was a hybrid that could be played at home or on the go, and it became one of the best-selling consoles ever.
When these Nintendo machines launched.Nintendo Switch 2: The Switch 2 is the successor of the Switch, with a larger screen, and has a backward compatible library.

How long these took to cross the Atlanti.Mayflower (1620): Storms and poor navigation left its 102 passengers at Cape Cod, far from the Virginia territory they were licensed to settle.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.Columbus from the Canaries: He made a last stop at La Gomera in the Canaries to resupply before the open Atlantic, riding the trade winds west.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.SS Great Western (1838): Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed it, and it was the first steamship built specifically for regular transatlantic passenger service.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.RMS Mauretania (1909): It held the Blue Riband for the fastest Atlantic crossing for about 20 years, until 1929.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.SS United States (1952): Its 1952 maiden voyage set Blue Riband records that no passenger liner has beaten since.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.Lindbergh (1927): Lindbergh flew solo and nonstop from New York to Paris in the Spirit of St. Louis, winning the $25,000 Orteig Prize.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.Alcock and Brown (1919): The first nonstop transatlantic flight went from Newfoundland to Ireland, ending nose-first in a bog near Clifden.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.Boeing 747: Its upper-deck hump was designed so the jet could later become a freighter, since planners expected supersonic jets to take over passengers.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.Concorde: It cruised at twice the speed of sound, so passengers landing in New York could arrive earlier by the clock than they left London.
How long these took to cross the Atlanti.SR-71 record (1974): The Blackbird, flying over three times the speed of sound, set this New York to London record on 1 September 1974.

Vehicles by weight.Bicycle: Road bikes in UCI racing must weigh at least 6.8 kg, so teams sometimes add weights to bikes that come out lighter.
Vehicles by weight.Motorcycle: A sport bike can out-accelerate most cars thanks to its light weight and high power, which makes it quick but demanding to ride.
Vehicles by weight.Smart ForTwo: It is only about 2.7 m long, short enough to park nose-first at the curb, and its body is a rigid steel safety cell.
Vehicles by weight.Toyota Corolla: It is the best-selling nameplate in car history, with over 50 million sold since 1966, and it has been through twelve generations.
Vehicles by weight.Ford F-150: Its F-Series family has been America's best-selling truck for decades, and Ford sells many hundreds of thousands a year.
Vehicles by weight.GMC Hummer EV: Its battery alone weighs about 1,300 kg, so the rest of the vehicle weighs roughly as much as a small family car.
Vehicles by weight.School bus: American school-bus yellow was chosen in 1939 at a conference because it is easy to see in dawn and dusk light.
Vehicles by weight.Fully loaded US semi: The US federal limit is 80,000 lb, about 36 tonnes, for a loaded truck on the interstates, split across five axles.
Vehicles by weight.Diesel locomotive: A diesel locomotive's engine drives a generator that powers electric motors on the wheels, so it is really an electric train with a power plant on board.
Vehicles by weight.Boeing 747 at takeoff: A large share of that weight at takeoff is fuel, and a jumbo jet can burn around 10 tonnes an hour in flight.

Supercontinents, past and future.Vaalbara: Named for South Africa's Kaapvaal and Australia's Pilbara cratons, whose ancient rocks match so well they may once have been joined.
Supercontinents, past and future.Ur: Possibly the first continent-sized landmass, Ur takes its name from the German word for primeval; some scientists doubt it was a true supercontinent.
Supercontinents, past and future.Kenorland: Named after the Kenoran mountain-building event, it is hypothetical, inferred from matching ancient rock records on several cratons.
Supercontinents, past and future.Columbia (Nuna): Also called Nuna, from an Inuit word for land; its core of ancient cratons later became part of Rodinia.
Supercontinents, past and future.Rodinia: Its name is thought to come from the Russian for motherland, and its breakup may have helped trigger the 'Snowball Earth' ice ages.
Supercontinents, past and future.Pannotia: A debated, short-lived supercontinent that may have formed just before the Cambrian burst of animal life; the name means 'all southern'.
Supercontinents, past and future.Gondwana: The great southern landmass joined Africa, South America, India, Australia and Antarctica; it is named after a region of central India.
Supercontinents, past and future.Pangaea: Its name means 'all the Earth' in Greek; matching fossils like Mesosaurus in South America and Africa helped prove it existed.
Supercontinents, past and future.Laurasia breaks away: When Pangaea split, Laurasia was the northern half, later becoming North America, Europe and most of Asia, while Gondwana stayed south.
Supercontinents, past and future.Pangaea Proxima (predicted): One predicted future landmass, from Christopher Scotese's model; rivals like Amasia and Novopangaea disagree by tens of millions of years.

Galaxies and beyond by distance.Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy: This small galaxy is being torn apart by the Milky Way's gravity, its stars stretched into streams that wrap around our own galaxy.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.Large Magellanic Cloud: Visible to the naked eye from the Southern Hemisphere, it hosted Supernova 1987A, the nearest observed supernova in centuries.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.Small Magellanic Cloud: Magellan's crew noted it on their voyage, and Henrietta Leavitt used its variable stars to find a way to measure cosmic distances.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.Andromeda Galaxy: It's heading toward us and is expected to collide with the Milky Way in about four to five billion years; you can see it unaided.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.Centaurus A: A dark dust lane splits this galaxy, the likely result of a merger, and it hosts a supermassive black hole firing out jets.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.Whirlpool Galaxy: In 1845 Lord Rosse sketched its spiral shape through his huge telescope, the first spiral structure ever seen in a galaxy.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.M87: Its supermassive black hole became the first ever imaged, by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.Coma Cluster: In the 1930s Fritz Zwicky saw its galaxies moving too fast to be held together by visible matter, an early hint of dark matter.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.Quasar 3C 273: In 1963 Maarten Schmidt found its enormous redshift, the first quasar identified; it outshines hundreds of ordinary galaxies.
Galaxies and beyond by distance.Galaxy GN-z11: Light from it has travelled 13.4 billion years, so we see it as it was when the universe was only about 400 million years old.

Roman numerals by value.XIX: Romans had no symbol for zero, so their counting began at I, and subtraction pairs like IX made nine fit in two letters.
Roman numerals by value.XLIX: The Romans wrote 49 as XLIX, which is XL for forty plus IX for nine, not the shorter IL, which isn't standard.
Roman numerals by value.LXXX: It uses the maximum of three X's in a row; add one more and the Romans switched to subtraction, writing XC for ninety.
Roman numerals by value.XC: Rather than LXXXX, the Romans wrote ninety as XC, ten less than a hundred, and C comes from centum, Latin for hundred.
Roman numerals by value.CXL: The C in this numeral comes from centum, Latin for a hundred, which is also the root of century and cent.
Roman numerals by value.CD: The D in this numeral stands for 500, which began as half of an older Etruscan symbol for a thousand.
Roman numerals by value.DCCC: The D stands for 500, and eight hundred is the first value below 1,000 written with three same-letter repeats.
Roman numerals by value.CM: The M stands for mille, Latin for thousand, which gave us 'mile', originally a thousand paces.
Roman numerals by value.MCM: Film credits and the Super Bowl keep Roman numerals alive, so a year such as this one often turns up in copyright dates.
Roman numerals by value.MMXXIV: Roman numerals get long fast: 3,888, MMMDCCCLXXXVIII, is the longest below 4,000, at 15 letters, and this is the Paris Olympics year.

Medical milestones of the 21st century.Gleevec targeted cancer drug: Imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a deadly disease into a manageable one for most patients.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.Stem cells from skin (iPS): Shinya Yamanaka showed adult cells could be reprogrammed into stem cells, and won a Nobel Prize in 2012.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.First full face transplant: Surgeons at Vall d'Hebron hospital in Barcelona performed it, restoring a patient's face after an accident.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.CRISPR gene editing paper: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier's paper showed bacterial machinery could edit DNA, earning them the 2020 Nobel Prize.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.Sovaldi cures hepatitis C: Sofosbuvir cured the large majority of hepatitis C cases with pills, but its price per pill caused controversy.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.CAR-T cancer therapy approved: Kymriah was the first approved therapy that engineers a patient's own T cells to attack leukemia.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.Ebola vaccine approved: Ervebo became the first Ebola vaccine approved by US regulators, after trials during the DRC outbreak.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.AlphaFold predicts proteins: DeepMind's AI predicted protein shapes at a level close to experiments, and won a share of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.Wegovy approved for weight: This semaglutide drug is similar to the diabetes medicine Ozempic and helped spark a boom in weight-loss drugs.
Medical milestones of the 21st century.Casgevy CRISPR therapy: The UK approved it first, for sickle cell disease, making it the first licensed CRISPR therapy.

US Army officer ranks.Second Lieutenant: It is the lowest commissioned rank, marked by a single gold bar, and a platoon leader often holds it.
US Army officer ranks.First Lieutenant: A single silver bar marks this rank, usually reached after about two years as a lieutenant.
US Army officer ranks.Captain: It's marked by two silver bars, and a captain often commands a company of 100 or more soldiers.
US Army officer ranks.Major: The oak leaf insignia is gold, and these officers typically serve as staff officers in a battalion.
US Army officer ranks.Lieutenant Colonel: The oak leaf insignia here is silver, and they usually command a battalion of several hundred soldiers.
US Army officer ranks.Colonel: It is marked by a silver eagle and often commands a brigade, and it's the rank just below the stars.
US Army officer ranks.Brigadier General: It has one star, sometimes called the 'one-star general', and it is the first of the general officer ranks.
US Army officer ranks.Major General: It has two stars, and typically leads a division of roughly ten to fifteen thousand soldiers.
US Army officer ranks.Lieutenant General: It has three stars and commands a corps, a formation of tens of thousands of soldiers.
US Army officer ranks.General: Four stars mark it, and the five-star rank is reserved for wartime, last held by Omar Bradley.

How much of each is water.Cucumber: Nearly all water, with so few calories that a whole one has about 45. Its flesh is famously cool, which gave rise to the phrase "cool as a cucumber".
How much of each is water.Watermelon: Wild watermelons come from southern Africa, where they were valued as a water source. Today's sweet red fruit is the result of long breeding.
How much of each is water.Whole milk: Milk is mostly water but looks creamy because fat and protein droplets scatter light, which is why skim looks bluer than whole.
How much of each is water.Banana: Botanically a berry, though a strawberry is not. Bananas are slightly radioactive from potassium-40, which is harmless at food levels.
How much of each is water.Cooked chicken breast: Cooking drives water out, so a chicken breast can lose about a quarter of its weight in the oven, which is why overcooked chicken is so dry.
How much of each is water.White bread: Baking removes much of the water, leaving a firm crumb. Bread goes stale mostly because starch crystallizes, not because it dries out.
How much of each is water.Honey: Honey is so low in water and so sugar-heavy that bacteria can't thrive in it, so sealed honey can last for thousands of years.
How much of each is water.Uncooked white rice: Uncooked rice is dry, which is why it can be stored for years. As it cooks it absorbs roughly two to three times its volume of water.
How much of each is water.Almonds: Almonds are seeds of a fruit related to the peach, and they are very dry for the plant world, which is why they stay crisp.
How much of each is water.Granulated sugar: Refined sugar is pure sucrose with almost no water, which is why it keeps indefinitely and draws moisture from the air if left open.

Plants by number of chromosomes.Haplopappus gracilis: A small North American relative of the daisy with just two chromosome pairs, it was a favorite for studying chromosomes under the microscope.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Thale cress: A tiny weed related to mustard, it was the first plant to have its genome sequenced, in 2000, and is the lab rat of plant biology.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Garden pea: Gregor Mendel's garden pea has seven pairs of chromosomes, and his experiments, published in 1866, became the foundation of genetics.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Maize: Maize has 10 pairs. Barbara McClintock discovered "jumping genes" in its kernels, work that earned her a Nobel Prize in 1983.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Rice: Rice, one of the world's main food crops, has 12 pairs. Its genome was one of the first of any crop plant to be sequenced.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Bread wheat: Modern bread wheat is a hexaploid, with six sets of chromosomes, formed by two crossbreedings of wild grasses thousands of years ago.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Potato: Potatoes are usually tetraploid, with four sets of chromosomes, which makes breeding new varieties slow and complicated.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Garden strawberry: Garden strawberries carry eight sets of chromosomes, a result of two wild American species crossing in European gardens in the 1700s.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Sugarcane: Sugarcane has a huge, messy genome, with different sets of chromosomes that are hard to count, because modern types are hybrids of wild and cultivated species.
Plants by number of chromosomes.Adder's-tongue fern: This fern's chromosome count is the highest known in any living thing, thanks to repeated genome duplications over its evolution.

From your scalp down to your brain.Skin: The outermost layer of the scalp holds hair follicles and many oil glands, and it's a common place for cysts.
From your scalp down to your brain.Dense connective tissue: This dense layer is rich in blood vessels, and the vessels are held open by the tissue, which is why scalp wounds bleed so heavily.
From your scalp down to your brain.Galea aponeurotica: This tough sheet links the muscles of the forehead and the back of the head, and it can slide over the skull.
From your scalp down to your brain.Loose areolar tissue: This layer is called the danger zone because infections can spread through it into the skull's veins.
From your scalp down to your brain.Pericranium: A thin membrane that covers the outside of the skull bones and is attached firmly at the suture lines.
From your scalp down to your brain.Skull bone: The skull of a newborn has gaps called fontanelles that allow the plates to flex during birth.
From your scalp down to your brain.Dura mater: The toughest of the three membranes around the brain, and it contains large channels that drain blood.
From your scalp down to your brain.Arachnoid mater: Its name means spider-like, from the web-like strands that connect it to the layer beneath.
From your scalp down to your brain.Pia mater: This delicate membrane clings tightly to the brain's surface and follows every groove.
From your scalp down to your brain.Cerebral cortex: This outer sheet of the brain is only a few millimeters thick, yet it's where most conscious thought takes place.

Silly days on the calendar.Groundhog Day: The American holiday is when a groundhog in Pennsylvania predicts the weather, and it is based on a German tradition.
Silly days on the calendar.Pi Day: The date is written 3/14, and it also happens to be Albert Einstein's birthday, and some celebrate with pie.
Silly days on the calendar.April Fools' Day: The origins are unclear, but it may be linked to the switch to a new calendar in France, and pranks are traditional.
Silly days on the calendar.Star Wars Day: The date is a pun on 'May the Fourth be with you', and Lucasfilm officially celebrates it.
Silly days on the calendar.Towel Day: The day honours Douglas Adams, and fans carry a towel in honour of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
Silly days on the calendar.World Emoji Day: The day was launched by Jeremy Burge, and the date was chosen because the calendar emoji shows July 17.
Silly days on the calendar.International Cat Day: The day is a celebration of felines, and it was founded by the International Fund for Animal Welfare.
Silly days on the calendar.Talk Like a Pirate Day: The day was created by two friends in 1995 and spread when Dave Barry wrote about it.
Silly days on the calendar.Mole Day: Chemists celebrate the day, which marks Avogadro's number, 6.02 times 10 to the 23rd, from 6:02 am to 6:02 pm.
Silly days on the calendar.Festivus: The date was made up by a writer's father, and it was popularised by the TV show Seinfeld, and it has an aluminium pole.

British TV comedies by first broadcast.Steptoe and Son: The tale of two rag-and-bone men inspired the American hit Sanford and Son.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.Dad's Army: Its Home Guard characters made affectionate comedy of wartime England, and the show ran for nine years.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.Monty Python's Flying Circus: Its famous sketch about a tinned meat gave the world the word 'spam' for junk email.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.Fawlty Towers: John Cleese based Basil on a real Torquay hotelier, and only twelve episodes were ever made.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.Only Fools and Horses: Del Boy's tumble through a bar hatch is often voted one of the funniest moments in British television.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.Blackadder: Each series moved to a different era, and the last ended with a poignant charge over the top in the First World War.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.Mr. Bean: It barely uses dialogue, which helped it sell across the world, from Britain to Asia and Latin America.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.Absolutely Fabulous: Jennifer Saunders grew it from a sketch with Dawn French, and its catchphrase 'sweetie darling' became everyday slang.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.The Office (UK): Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant made just fourteen episodes, then saw the format remade in numerous countries.
British TV comedies by first broadcast.Peep Show: It was filmed through the characters' eyes, with their private thoughts in voiceover, and ran for nine series.

How light travels from the world to your.Cornea: This clear dome does about two thirds of the eye's focusing and has no blood vessels, taking its oxygen straight from the air.
How light travels from the world to your.Aqueous humor: This watery fluid is constantly replenished, and poor drainage raises eye pressure, which is the cause of glaucoma.
How light travels from the world to your.Pupil: It is not a thing but a hole in the iris, and it looks black because most light entering it is absorbed inside the eye.
How light travels from the world to your.Lens: It changes shape to focus close up, but stiffens with age, which is why most people need reading glasses in their forties.
How light travels from the world to your.Vitreous humor: This clear jelly fills most of the eyeball, and the specks drifting in it cast the 'floaters' many people notice.
How light travels from the world to your.Retina: It holds about 120 million rod cells and 6 million cone cells, and the image that lands on it is upside down.
How light travels from the world to your.Optic nerve: Each carries about a million fibers, and where it leaves the retina there are no light sensors, creating your blind spot.
How light travels from the world to your.Optic chiasm: Here half the fibers from each eye switch sides, so each half of the brain sees the opposite side of your view.
How light travels from the world to your.Thalamus: A relay hub deep in the brain, it passes signals from nearly all senses on to the cortex, with smell the main exception.
How light travels from the world to your.Visual cortex: At the back of the head, it processes edges, motion and color, and damage there can cause blindness even with healthy eyes.

When these great buildings were finished.Great Pyramid of Giza: Built from about 2.3 million blocks, its sides line up almost perfectly with the compass points.
When these great buildings were finished.Parthenon: Its columns bulge slightly in the middle and lean inward, subtle curves that make the temple look perfectly straight.
When these great buildings were finished.Colosseum: It could seat roughly 50,000 and had a huge retractable awning to shade the crowds.
When these great buildings were finished.Pantheon, Rome: Its unreinforced concrete dome is still the world's largest, and a hole in the roof lights the interior.
When these great buildings were finished.Hagia Sophia: Built in under six years, it has been a cathedral, a mosque, a museum and a mosque again.
When these great buildings were finished.Angkor Wat: The world's largest religious monument, it was built as a Hindu temple and is on Cambodia's flag.
When these great buildings were finished.Forbidden City: Home to 24 emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties for almost 500 years, and its name means it was closed to ordinary people.
When these great buildings were finished.St. Peter's Basilica: It is among the largest church interiors ever, and Michelangelo designed its dome.
When these great buildings were finished.Taj Mahal complex: Shah Jahan built it as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, and construction took about two decades.
When these great buildings were finished.St. Paul's Cathedral: Christopher Wren's masterpiece rose after the Great Fire of London, and it survived the Blitz.

Holiday islands by area.Mustique: A tiny private island in the Grenadines where Princess Margaret had a house.
Holiday islands by area.Bora Bora: Its volcanic peak, Mount Otemanu, rises from a ring of lagoon and reef.
Holiday islands by area.Santorini: A giant eruption here in about 1600 BC created its flooded caldera, and may have inspired the legend of Atlantis.
Holiday islands by area.Barbados: The easternmost island of the Caribbean, and one of its most densely populated.
Holiday islands by area.Phuket: Thailand's largest island, joined to the mainland by a bridge.

How long can it live?.Adult mayfly: Adult mayflies have no working mouths and live only to mate; the nymphs, however, can spend a year or more underwater.
How long can it live?.Housefly: Houseflies taste with their feet and lay hundreds of eggs, so populations explode quickly in warm weather.
How long can it live?.Hamster: Hamsters are mostly nocturnal and stash food in their cheek pouches, which stretch to carry astonishing loads.
How long can it live?.Cat: Cats spend about two-thirds of their lives asleep, and the oldest on record, Creme Puff, reached 38.
How long can it live?.Horse: Horses can doze standing up thanks to a locking mechanism in their legs, and many live to 25 or 30.
How long can it live?.Elephant: Herds are led by the oldest female, the matriarch, who remembers water holes through droughts.
How long can it live?.Galápagos tortoise: Some individuals have passed 150 years; 'Lonesome George' was the last known Pinta Island tortoise when he died in 2012.
How long can it live?.Bowhead whale: Old stone harpoon tips found embedded in some bowheads show that individuals have lived through well over a century.
How long can it live?.Greenland shark: It grows only about a centimetre a year, and females may not breed until they are around 150 years old.
How long can it live?.Ocean quahog clam: A clam nicknamed Ming, dredged off Iceland, was aged at 507 by its growth rings, so it was born before Shakespeare's grandparents.

Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Clavicle: The collarbone's Latin name means "little key", and it is the most commonly broken bone in the body.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Scapula: The shoulder blade connects to the body only through muscle, with no joint attaching it to the ribs.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Humerus: The funny bone isn't a bone at all; the tingle comes from the ulnar nerve running near the humerus's elbow end.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Radius: This forearm bone crosses over the ulna when you turn your palm, and it can rotate on the ulna.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Scaphoid: The boat-shaped wrist bone is the most often broken carpal, and it heals slowly because blood supply is poor.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Trapezoid: One of eight small wrist bones, it is shaped like a wedge and lies beside the trapezium, at the base of the index finger.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Second metacarpal: The long bone of the palm below the index finger, it is one of five that fan out like spokes from the wrist.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Proximal phalanx: Phalanx is the Greek word for a battle line, since finger bones line up in rows.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Middle phalanx: The thumb lacks one, but the index finger has three phalanges, with this one in between.
Bones from shoulder to index fingertip.Distal phalanx: This fingertip bone supports the nail bed, and it is the smallest bone of the finger.

How long these ancient units of length w.Roman digit: The digit was a finger's width in the Roman system, and the Roman inch (uncia) was a twelfth of a foot.
How long these ancient units of length w.Roman palm: A palm was the width of four fingers, and it's the same idea as the modern hand measure used for horses.
How long these ancient units of length w.Roman foot: The Roman foot was slightly shorter than the modern one, and it's the origin of the English foot.
How long these ancient units of length w.Egyptian royal cubit: The royal cubit was the length from the elbow to the fingertips; the Great Pyramid's builders used it, and measuring rods were made of granite.
How long these ancient units of length w.Roman pace: A pace in Rome meant two steps, a full stride from one heel strike to the same heel's next strike.
How long these ancient units of length w.Greek stadion: The stadion was the length of a foot race at Olympia, and it gave us the word stadium.
How long these ancient units of length w.Chinese li (Han era): The li is a traditional Chinese unit that was redefined many times, and today it is standardized as half a kilometer.
How long these ancient units of length w.Roman mile: The word mile comes from mille passus, 'a thousand paces', which were Roman marching steps.
How long these ancient units of length w.Gallic league: The league was the distance a person could walk in about an hour, and the Gauls, who ruled France, used it.
How long these ancient units of length w.Persian parasang: A parasang was the distance a person could walk in an hour in ancient Persia, and Greek writers like Xenophon used it.

Disney princesses by their film debut.Snow White: Snow White was Disney's first full-length animated film, and the studio's staff nicknamed it 'Disney's Folly' before it became a smash hit.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Cinderella: Cinderella saved Disney after years of financial troubles, and the story's glass slipper may be a mistranslation of fur.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Aurora: Aurora has only about 18 minutes of screen time and few lines, even though the film is named Sleeping Beauty after her.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Ariel: Ariel's film The Little Mermaid started the Disney Renaissance, and her red hair was inspired by actress Alyssa Milano.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Belle: Belle was the first animated film nominated for Best Picture, and it was Disney's first to become a Broadway musical.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Jasmine: Jasmine's story is set in a fictional Arabian city, and her tiger Rajah was named after a Hindi word for king.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Pocahontas: Pocahontas was based on a real woman, born around 1596, though the film departs heavily from history.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Mulan: Mulan is based on the Chinese legend of Hua Mulan, a girl who disguised herself as a man to take her father's place in the army.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Tiana: Tiana was Disney's first Black princess, and the film The Princess and the Frog was set in New Orleans.
Disney princesses by their film debut.Moana: Moana's film involved Polynesian cultural consultants, and the voyaging tradition it shows is real, as islanders crossed the Pacific by stars and waves.

Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Euchre: Euchre is credited with giving us the joker: it was first added as a top trump card in 1860s American decks.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Skat: Germany's national card game, invented in Altenburg in the early 1800s; three players bid, and two cards go face down as the skat.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Pinochle: Pinochle uses two copies of every card from nine to ace, and its bid-and-meld play grew out of the European game Bezique.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Standard deck (no jokers): The French-suited 52-card deck took hold in 15th-century France; it can be shuffled into about 8 x 10^67 orders, so a good shuffle is almost surely unique.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Spot It! (Dobble): Any two cards share exactly one symbol, a trick of finite geometry; the game was created in France under the name Dobble.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Rook: Parker Brothers made Rook in 1906 for families who disapproved of ordinary playing cards; its deck has four colored suits plus one Rook bird card.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Tarot: Tarot began as an Italian trick-taking game in the 1400s; its 22 trump cards were only later adopted for fortune-telling.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Set: Each card differs in four features: number, shape, color and shading. The largest group of cards with no valid Set in it is 20.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Phase 10: A rummy-style game from 1982 in which you must complete ten set-collecting goals in order, from two sets of three to a run of ten-plus.
Cards (or tiles) in these game decks.Mahjong (with flowers): The set includes bonus flower and season tiles; the game took modern form in 19th-century China and became a craze in 1920s America.

How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.Earth forms: The planet formed from a dusty disk around the young Sun, and a giant impact soon after likely made the Moon.
How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.First dinosaurs: The first were small, two-legged meat-eaters such as Eoraptor, in the Triassic.
How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.Dinosaurs wiped out: A roughly 10 km asteroid struck at Chicxulub, Mexico; birds are living dinosaurs.
How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.First Homo sapiens: Fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, pushed back the date of our species to about 300,000 years.
How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.Lascaux cave paintings: Teenagers found the cave in southwestern France in 1940, with over 600 painted animals.
How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.Stonehenge begun: It began as a circular ditch and bank; its large sarsen stones came around 2500 BC.
How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.Western Roman Empire falls: The last emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed by the Germanic general Odoacer.
How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.Moon landing: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent about two and a half hours walking on the surface.
How long ago? From the Big Bang to the i.First iPhone: Steve Jobs unveiled it in January 2007; over two billion have been sold since.

Asian islands by area.Taiwan: Taiwan is about the size of Belgium, and its highest peak, Yushan, is nearly 4,000 meters tall.
Asian islands by area.Sri Lanka: Sri Lanka is shaped like a teardrop, and it's long been known as the world's top tea and cinnamon producer.
Asian islands by area.Hokkaido: Hokkaido is Japan's northernmost main island, and it's famed for its snowfall and powdery ski slopes.
Asian islands by area.Mindanao: Mindanao is the second-largest island in the Philippines, and it has Mount Apo, the country's highest peak.
Asian islands by area.Luzon: Luzon is the Philippines' largest island, and Manila, the capital, lies on it.
Asian islands by area.Java: Java has more than a hundred volcanoes, and it holds roughly half of Indonesia's people.
Asian islands by area.Sulawesi: Sulawesi has a strange shape like an orchid or letter K, and it's home to unusual animals like the anoa dwarf buffalo.
Asian islands by area.Honshu: Honshu is the seventh largest island in the world, and the Shinkansen bullet train was first built here.
Asian islands by area.Sumatra: Sumatra is home to orangutans, tigers and elephants, and it holds the world's largest flower, the Rafflesia.
Asian islands by area.Borneo: Borneo is shared by three countries, Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei, and it's one of the oldest rainforests in the world.

Getting around on land and water: when t.Steam locomotive (Trevithick): Richard Trevithick's Welsh locomotive hauled iron along the Penydarren tramway, though it was so heavy it broke the cast-iron rails.
Getting around on land and water: when t.Draisine running machine: Karl von Drais's wooden two-wheeler had no pedals; riders pushed along with their feet. It was the ancestor of the bicycle.
Getting around on land and water: when t.London Underground: The Metropolitan Railway opened in January 1863 as the first underground passenger railway, hauled by steam locomotives.
Getting around on land and water: when t.Electric tram (Siemens): Werner von Siemens opened the world's first electric tram line in Berlin-Lichterfelde.
Getting around on land and water: when t.Rover safety bicycle: John Kemp Starley's Rover, with equal-sized wheels and chain drive, set the template for the modern bicycle.
Getting around on land and water: when t.Benz Patent-Motorwagen: Karl Benz's three-wheeler was patented in January 1886. Its single-cylinder engine made less than one horsepower.
Getting around on land and water: when t.Pneumatic tyre (Dunlop): Scottish vet John Boyd Dunlop made air-filled tyres for his son's tricycle, making rides far smoother.
Getting around on land and water: when t.Hovercraft: Christopher Cockerell tested the idea with tin cans and a vacuum cleaner. The SR.N1 crossed the Channel in 1959.
Getting around on land and water: when t.Japanese bullet train: Opened just before the Tokyo Olympics, the Tokaido Shinkansen has never had a passenger fatality from a derailment or collision.
Getting around on land and water: when t.Segway: Dean Kamen's self-balancing scooter was hyped as reinventing cities. Production of its original model ended in 2020.

How many digits?.Bank card PIN: Four digits give 10,000 combinations, yet 1234 and 0000 are so overused that they are among the first codes thieves try.
How many digits?.US ZIP code: The Zone Improvement Plan code launched in 1963, and the extra four digits of ZIP+4 came in 1983.
How many digits?.US Social Security number: Created in 1936, it once encoded geographic area in its first digits; since 2011 numbers are issued randomly.
How many digits?.US phone number: Introduced with the 1947 North American Numbering Plan, three-digit area codes made direct long-distance dialing possible.
How many digits?.UK mobile number: All start with 07, a prefix dropped when dialing from abroad with the +44 code.
How many digits?.UPC barcode: The first product scanned was a pack of Wrigley's gum in Troy, Ohio, in 1974.
How many digits?.European EAN barcode: It extends the American UPC with one extra digit, and the leading digits show where the code was registered, not where the item was made.
How many digits?.Phone IMEI number: Dial *#06# on most phones to see it; networks use it to block stolen handsets.
How many digits?.Visa card number: Every Visa number starts with 4, and its final digit is a check digit computed with the Luhn algorithm to catch typos.
How many digits?.UK IBAN (characters): IBAN length varies by country: Norway's is just 15 characters, and the UK's mixes letters with digits.

Long things, end to end.Golden Gate Bridge: The San Francisco landmark opened in 1937 and is painted International Orange, not gold. It was the longest suspension bridge in the world until 1964.
Long things, end to end.Loch Ness: This Scottish loch holds more fresh water than all the lakes of England and Wales combined. It is deep and murky, which fuels the monster legends.
Long things, end to end.Hadrian's Wall: The Roman emperor Hadrian ordered it built across northern Britain around AD 122. Soldiers manned small forts called milecastles along its length.
Long things, end to end.Suez Canal: Opened in 1869, it links the Mediterranean and Red seas without locks, cutting thousands of kilometres from journeys between Europe and Asia.
Long things, end to end.Grand Canyon: The Colorado River carved it over millions of years, and in places it is over a mile deep. Its rock layers reveal nearly two billion years of geology.
Long things, end to end.English Channel: The strip of sea between England and France is only about 33 km wide at the narrowest. Captain Matthew Webb first swam across it in 1875.
Long things, end to end.Great Barrier Reef: Built by billions of tiny coral polyps, it is the largest living structure on Earth and is visible from space. It lies off Queensland, Australia.
Long things, end to end.Appalachian Trail: This hiking path runs through 14 US states from Georgia to Maine. Only a small share of those who attempt a full end-to-end walk finish it.
Long things, end to end.Andes mountains: The longest continental mountain range runs down the west of South America. Its peaks include Aconcagua, the highest outside Asia.
Long things, end to end.Trans-Siberian Railway: The world's longest railway line crosses eight time zones between Moscow and Vladivostok. A full journey takes about a week.

Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.Henry VI, Part 1: Often considered among his earliest history plays, it features Joan of Arc, and some scholars think other writers helped write it.
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.Romeo and Juliet: Shakespeare based his tragedy on an earlier poem, yet his version compresses the story into just a few days.
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.The Merchant of Venice: The play's complex moneylender Shylock still sparks debate, and its 'quality of mercy' speech is among the best known.
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.Julius Caesar: It may have been among the first plays performed at the Globe Theatre, which opened in 1599 on the Thames.
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.Hamlet: At roughly 30,000 words, it is Shakespeare's longest play and contains the line 'To be, or not to be.'
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.Twelfth Night: Its title refers to the festival ending Christmas, and the plot of mistaken identity centers on twins separated by a shipwreck.
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.Othello: Iago's cunning manipulation drives this tragedy of jealousy, and Iago has more lines than the title character.
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.Macbeth: Theater people superstitiously avoid saying its name inside a theater, calling it 'the Scottish play' instead.
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.Antony and Cleopatra: Shakespeare drew heavily on Plutarch's account, and the play ranges across Rome and Egypt in dozens of short scenes.
Shakespeare's plays, by when they were w.The Tempest: Often counted among his last solo plays, it's set on a magical island, and Prospero's farewell is often read as Shakespeare's own.

Pregnancy lengths of animals.Hamster: Syrian hamsters carry their pups for just over two weeks, among the shortest of any placental mammal, and pups are born hairless.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Mouse: A female mouse can become pregnant again almost immediately after giving birth, producing many litters in a single year.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Rabbit: Rabbits can conceive again within hours of giving birth, a trait that helped give them their reputation for rapid breeding.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Dog: Dogs carry pups for about nine weeks, and a vet can often feel or detect puppies by around the fourth week.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Pig: The old farmer's rule of 'three months, three weeks and three days' gives a pig's gestation, which is close to 114 days.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Sheep: Ewes usually give birth to one or two lambs, and lambing is timed so lambs arrive in spring when grass is growing.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Human: Pregnancy is counted from the last menstrual period, not conception, so the doctor's due date adds about two extra weeks.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Horse: A mare carries her foal for about eleven months, and foals can stand and run within hours of birth.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Giraffe: Calves are born standing up and fall nearly two meters to the ground, and they can stand within about an hour.
Pregnancy lengths of animals.Elephant: The longest of any land mammal, nearly twenty-two months, with the baby born weighing around 100 kilograms.
